records.text: Candace Owens said Frank Zach Turek worked at the Pentagon as Deputy Division Chief of the Joint Staff.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Zach (Frank Zach Turek) was working at the Pentagon. He is today employed in Washington, D.C. at the Pentagon, serving as the Deputy Division Chief of the Joint Staff.

verification.notes: Frank Zachary Turek public professional profile identifies him as a U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel who completed a three-year assignment on the Joint Staff at the Pentagon. Public employment listings identify the role as Deputy Division Chief. His current profile says he has since moved to the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, so the claim is verified as a past position rather than a current one.

records.text: Candace Owens said Frank Turek did not call 9-1-1 or phone his son who worked for the Department of Defense.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Frank (Frank Turek) didn't call 9-1-1, nor did he think to phone his son who works for the most powerful, most funded and most corrupt division of our government, the Department of Defense.

verification.notes: Public interviews say the security party called 911, but the available released calls and reporting do not identify which member made the call. No reliable public phone record establishes whether Frank Turek personally called 911 or contacted his Department of Defense-employed son. Absence of that evidence is not evidence that the calls did not occur, so the accusation is attempted and unverifiable rather than false.

sources.title: SRS 254 Brian Harpole interview
sources.relevance: Harpole says the party called 911 but does not identify the caller, leaving the accusation unresolved.
